Prepare Review Subsets from Person and Class Incident Reports

prepareSubsetInfo.Rd

Translate long incident reports or explicit issue specifications into exact person–item pairs for visualSubsetRecode. Long incidents use class membership from the response data and each person's booklet. Incident provenance is retained when reports overlap.

Usage

prepareSubsetInfo(dat, issues = NULL, persons = NULL, booklets = NULL,
                  blocks = NULL, rotation = NULL, subunits = NULL,
                  ID = "ID", classID = "classId", incidents = NULL,
                  unmatched = c("drop", "error"),
                  dataLevel = c("subunit", "unit"))

# S3 method for class 'preparedSubsetInfo'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

dat

A nonempty data frame of wide responses: one row per person and one column per response, with unique, nonmissing, nonblank person IDs. For incidents, also include nonmissing, nonblank class IDs unless classID = NULL. Response values may be NA.

issues

NULL (default) or a nonempty data frame for the explicit issue workflow. Supply exactly one of issues and incidents. An issues table has one row per issue and these columns:

issueId

Unique, nonmissing, nonblank incident identifier.

level

Character entries: "person" or "class".

targetId

Nonmissing, nonblank person ID or class ID, according to level.

scope

Character entries: "item", "block", or "blockPosition".

target

A single item name, block name, or positive integer block position, according to scope. Item targets use subunit/recoded names in subunit mode and unit names in unit mode. A character column accommodates mixed scopes.

comment

Optional description; missing comments are allowed.

persons

NULL (default) or a nonempty legacy class-membership data frame for issues, with columns named by ID and classID and one row per person. IDs must be nonmissing and nonblank; person IDs must be unique. With NULL, class issues use the membership in dat. Do not supply this argument with incidents. Class IDs must identify classes uniquely across schools.

booklets

NULL (default) or a booklet-design data frame with a unique booklet identifier and columns block1, block2, etc. Column suffixes determine positions, regardless of column order. Entries are block identifiers; empty or missing entries represent unoccupied positions. Required together with blocks and rotation for incidents and for issues with scope "block" or "blockPosition". All three may be NULL for item-only issues.

blocks

NULL (default) or a block-design data frame with block, subunit, and subunitBlockPosition. Positions must be positive, finite whole numbers, such as 1, 2, or their character equivalents. Items and positions must be unique within each relevant block. Required whenever booklets is required.

rotation

NULL (default) or a person-to-booklet data frame with columns named by ID and booklet, with one row per person. Required whenever booklets is required.

subunits

NULL (default) or a mapping data frame with unique subunit, optional subunitRecoded names and unit assignments, normally inputList$subunits. Required in unit mode, including the unit column. Supply the complete table from the same input list as the design tables so single-subunit units can be identified. In subunit mode, NULL permits matching original subunit names directly to data columns.

ID

A single nonempty character string naming the person-ID column, e.g. "learner_key", shared by dat, incidents and rotation. Input columns are not renamed. Must differ from classID and reserved incident/output column names. Default: "ID". Supply a column name, not a vector of IDs.

classID

A single nonempty character string naming the class-ID column, normally in dat and incidents, or NULL. An example column name is "group_key"; default: "classId". Set NULL for individual data without classes; class reports are then forbidden. Also names the column in legacy persons.

incidents

NULL (default) or a nonempty long data frame with person ID, class ID and blockPosition. Column names for the IDs are supplied through ID and classID; classID = NULL removes the class column requirement. Block positions must be positive, finite whole numbers (numeric or character equivalents). Optional columns are issueId, level ("person" or "class") and comment. Supply this instead of issues and persons. See checkSubsetIncidents for the complete input contract.

unmatched

A single character string: "drop" (default for incidents) or "error". For incidents, "drop" excludes source rows with unknown persons/classes, with an informational message and retained report. "error" makes absent cases an error as well. On errors, an overview separates case matching from response resolution; the complete report is retained in condition$report. All other problems, including class mismatches and unresolved design, still stop preparation. Dropping every selection also raises an error. With issues, handling is always strict: omit this argument or use "error"; explicitly supplying "drop" is not allowed.

dataLevel

A single character string: "subunit" (default) or "unit". "subunit" resolves raw or recoded subunits; "unit" maps design subunits to aggregated units. Supply the same level to checkSubsetIncidents.

object

A preparedSubsetInfo data frame returned by prepareSubsetInfo.

...

Additional summary arguments; currently ignored.

Details

Long incident workflow. Each row of incidents describes a person–block-position pair, or a class–block-position pair with a missing person ID. Within each class all person IDs must be supplied or all must be missing. All-missing IDs select the entire class in dat; supplied IDs preserve the exact reported person–position pairs. No separate persons input is needed. Use checkSubsetIncidents to inspect the collected problems first. Preparation runs the same check automatically. Errors of class subsetIncidentError retain the report in condition$report. The report remains available on successful results as attr(info, "incidentCheck"), including any explicitly excluded rows. Input data are never modified by preparation or checking.

For incidents, the review uses only available response columns at the reported block positions. Design entries without a response column, including unmapped subunits with no original/recoded column match, are omitted. They remain in attr(info, "incidentCheck")$ignored. Additional metadata for unreported persons and positions does not block the selection. No unit names are guessed. Ambiguities affecting existing columns and unavailable design for a reported position remain errors. If no selections remain, preparation stops with an empty selection message and the report. This is separate from a comprehensive checkInputList or checkDesign check.

For long incidents, review defaults to one decision per class, or per person when classID = NULL. Pass useGroups = NULL explicitly to visualSubsetRecode to review individual persons even when classes are available. Multiple long rows for a person are combined. Grouping changes how selected cells are reviewed, not which cells are selected.

Subunits and units. Design tables always describe subunits. With dataLevel = "subunit", each selected subunit must resolve to exactly one original or recoded response column. With dataLevel = "unit", the mapping subunits$unit identifies the response: a unit-named column takes precedence. If that column is absent, a unit with exactly one subunit may use the original or recoded subunit name instead, supporting aggregateData(rename = FALSE). A single component column cannot replace a multi-subunit aggregate.

In unit mode, an incident affecting any subunit selects the entire unit for that person. Several subunits, including subunits at different block positions, can refer to the same response. The review displays and recodes it once; selecting any of its reported block positions also selects the entire unit. All source subunits and positions of selected responses remain in the prepared table. Missing mappings for existing response-column matches and different units resolving to the same data cell are errors.

Explicit issue workflow. The original issues format remains supported for item names, named blocks and block positions. Each issue has one unique issueId and one target, and reviews still default to grouping by issueId. Class issues select all members in persons, or dat when persons is omitted.

For block or block-position reports, supply all three design tables booklets, blocks, and rotation. A named block can appear at different positions for different people; a block position can refer to different blocks. Item-only reports do not require design tables. When design tables are supplied, item selections are also checked against each person's booklet.

For issues, the function stops on unknown classes, persons absent from dat, unresolved items, ambiguous mappings, and targets not administered to a selected person. It never silently drops class members or guesses assignments. Inspect and resolve these reports before starting a review. Empty report tables are rejected.

Numeric identifiers retain enough precision to distinguish the stored values throughout preparation and review. Character identifiers are matched exactly. Import identifiers as character when leading zeros or digits beyond numeric precision must be preserved; precision already lost during import cannot be recovered.

The returned table contains one row per incident/person/design subunit. In unit mode several rows can select one unit response. An overlapping cell appears once for each incident that selected it. There is no automatic priority between individual and class reports. In the explicit issues format each report selects one target. Different replacement values per incident are not implemented. Pausing, automatic checkpoints and resuming a review are provided by visualSubsetRecode.

Value

prepareSubsetInfo returns a data frame of class preparedSubsetInfo with columns issueId, the person ID, datCols, level, targetId, scope, target, block, blockPosition, subunitBlockPosition, and comment, plus booklet, subunit, subunitRecoded, unit, item, and itemStatus, mappingIssue, and ignoredReason. datCols identifies the response column, item the logical identifier at the chosen response level; successful rows have itemStatus = "matched". The ID column name and dataLevel are retained as attributes. Without design tables, block metadata is missing. Long incidents additionally retain sourceRow and the class ID (when used). Their attributes include classID, reviewGroup and incidentCheck.

Pass this object directly to visualSubsetRecode; the default grouping, ID column, comments, and available positions are selected automatically. summary returns a data frame with one row per incident, its level and target ID (comma-separated when several occur), counts of persons, items and distinct cells, and overlappingCells: the number of its cells also selected by another incident. Repeated rows of the same incident do not inflate cell or overlap counts. Counts include cells containing NA.

See also

visualSubsetRecode, inputList, vignette("subset_review", package = "eatPrep")

Examples

dat <- data.frame(ID = c("P1", "P2"), I1 = c(1, 0), I2 = c(0, 1))
persons <- data.frame(ID = c("P1", "P2"), classId = "K1")
booklets <- data.frame(booklet = c("X", "Y"),
                       block1 = c("A", "B"), block2 = c("B", "A"))
blocks <- data.frame(subunit = c("I1", "I2"), block = c("A", "B"),
                     subunitBlockPosition = 1)
rotation <- data.frame(ID = c("P1", "P2"), booklet = c("X", "Y"))
issues <- data.frame(
  issueId = c("V1", "V2"), level = c("class", "person"),
  targetId = c("K1", "P1"), scope = c("blockPosition", "item"),
  target = c("1", "I1"), comment = c("Audio failure", NA)
)
info <- prepareSubsetInfo(dat, issues, persons, booklets, blocks, rotation)
info
#>   issueId ID datCols  level targetId         scope target booklet block
#> 1      V1 P1      I1  class       K1 blockPosition      1       X     A
#> 2      V1 P2      I2  class       K1 blockPosition      1       Y     B
#> 3      V2 P1      I1 person       P1          item     I1       X     A
#>   blockPosition subunitBlockPosition       comment subunit subunitRecoded unit
#> 1             1                    1 Audio failure      I1           <NA> <NA>
#> 2             1                    1 Audio failure      I2           <NA> <NA>
#> 3             1                    1          <NA>      I1           <NA> <NA>
#>   item itemStatus mappingIssue ignoredReason
#> 1   I1    matched         <NA>          <NA>
#> 2   I2    matched         <NA>          <NA>
#> 3   I1    matched         <NA>          <NA>
summary(info)
#>   issueId  level targetId persons items cells overlappingCells
#> 1      V1  class       K1       2     2     2                1
#> 2      V2 person       P1       1     1     1                1
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
result <- visualSubsetRecode(dat, info, toRecodeVal = "mci")
result$dat
result$subsetInfo
} # }
